name: Footer
$status: PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed. Nothing in this file is a ruling. Built in Lane M of the s203-D2 PM-topology trial from itinerary row 81 ('Footer — Incl. doormat / mega-footer', Layout & containers, P2), verified genuinely absent first-hand.
purpose: The SITE FOOTER: the contentinfo landmark at the end of a page, carrying the link groups a reader goes looking for, the legal links a regulator requires, and the copyright line. Two forms — a doormat (mega-footer) for pages a reader browses, and a slim legal bar for authenticated application screens where a four-column mat would be in the way.
$vocabularyCollision: ★★ DECLARED BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, because this is the s202-D3 class — the class where Dave rejected a build because one word carried two meanings and every assertion stayed green. In this repo 'footer' ALREADY means the LAYOUT FOOTER of a container: Drawer's footer actions, Modals' dialog footer, Data-grid's pagination footer, Command-palette's hint bar. The gated ACTION-BAR describes itself, verbatim, as 'A footer bar that pins a screen/flow's actions'. This component is the OTHER footer — the document's end matter. The two can appear on the same screen (an Action-bar pinned above a site Footer) and they are not variants of one another. ⛔ IF THIS COMPONENT KEEPS THE NAME 'Footer' IT INHERITS THE COLLISION. Renaming is Dave's; nothing here renames anything.

$differsFromNeighbours.Links: Links owns the link ATOM and already ships .related, which its own source calls 'the footer / utility pattern' — a wrapping list of related links. Footer is the REGION that arranges them: the landmark, the named columns, the legal bar, the copyright, the rule that separates the page from its end matter. THE TELL: strip the landmark and the group headings from a Footer and what is left is a .related list, and it should be one. links.meta.json already declares context:footer with a Footer relationship — the component graph anticipated this component before it existed.
$differsFromNeighbours.Action-bar: See $vocabularyCollision. Action-bar pins the ACTIONS of a flow and belongs to the task; its contents change per screen. Footer is the end of the DOCUMENT and belongs to the site; its contents do not change per screen.
$differsFromNeighbours.Headers: The masthead sibling. A header carries wayfinding a reader is about to use; a footer carries the links they went looking for and the text the regulator requires. A doormat that simply duplicates the masthead is a doormat that has stopped being read.
$differsFromNeighbours.Navigations / Sidebar-nav: Those model STATE — current page, expansion, sections, disclosure. A doormat is flat and stateless; the only state it carries is aria-current="page", inherited from the Links atom unchanged.

props.name: form
props.$note: doormat = brand statement + back-to-top + named link columns + legal bar. slim = legal bar and copyright only. Which surfaces get which is a product decision and is NOT settled here.

props.name: groups
props.$note: Each group is a <nav> with aria-labelledby pointing at its own heading, so a screen-reader user gets four named navigation landmarks rather than one anonymous list of forty links. The specimen shows four groups; the auto-fit track floor is 180px.

props.name: backToTop
props.$note: The arrow link from the gated Links atom, rotated to point up, glyph byte-matched from arrows-and-chevrons/arrow-up.svg. 44px tall.

variants.name: doormat
variants.use: the end of a marketing or servicing page — the reader may still be looking for something

variants.name: slim
variants.use: the end of an authenticated application screen — the reader came to do one thing and is finishing it

brand.use: the short statement or brand line that opens a mega-footer, beside the back-to-top link

tokens.surface: surface/subtle — the footer band, so the end matter reads as a band rather than as more page
tokens.divider: divider/border/section — the 1px rule between the page and the footer
tokens.subdivider: divider/border/subsection — inside the footer, between the brand block, the mat and the legal bar

$finding-44px-cost: ⚠ EVERY footer link is a >= 44px target at EVERY width, not only when stacked. That is STRICTER than the gated Links .related pattern, which grows its targets only at <=420px, and it is a visible design cost: a four-column doormat with four links per column becomes measurably taller than the compact typographic ideal a footer usually aims for. The trade is a design decision, not a technicality — see $decisionsForDave 2. No gate reads the target token for hit area, so this was MEASURED in a real browser rather than assumed.
$finding-type-debt-conflict: ★★ 'COPY THE APPROVED ARTEFACT VERBATIM' AND 'ADD ZERO TO THE SHRINK-ONLY TYPE RATCHET' CONFLICT WHEN THE APPROVED ARTEFACT IS ITSELF IN DEBT. The gated Links atom writes font-weight:500 twice in its own CSS — on a.arrow and on a.lnk[aria-current="page"] — and those are exactly the raw declarations TYPE-002 counts. Copying them verbatim DROVE _validate_type_composites.py red on this file (measured #204: 2 violations). The emphasis therefore arrives here through canon/type.css's own .t-ed-body-small .em modifier, applied in the MARKUP (the T-D14 markup-class route): identical rendered weight, zero added debt. Links itself was NOT edited — it is a gated shared artefact and its two declarations are the BUILD-PM's to retire. THE DIVERGENCE FROM THE PARENT IS DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN.

accessibility.landmark: <footer role="contentinfo"> with an aria-label naming which footer it is ('Site footer' / 'Legal footer'), so a page carrying both a doormat and a slim bar does not present two anonymous contentinfo landmarks.
accessibility.grouping: Each link column is a <nav> with aria-labelledby pointing at its own visible heading. Forty links in one anonymous list is not navigable; four named landmarks are.
accessibility.currentPage: aria-current="page" marked by WEIGHT plus a persistent 2px underline — never colour alone. Inherited from the Links atom; the weight arrives by composite modifier rather than by raw declaration (see $finding-type-debt-conflict).
accessibility.linkText: Every link names its destination. No 'click here', no 'more', no 'read more' — the aca-004 class the snippet gate blocks.
accessibility.targetSize: Every link is a >= 44px target at every width. MEASURED, not assumed; no gate reads the target token for hit area.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: Links are distinguished by an underline, not by colour. No RAG value appears in this component at all.

antiPatterns: Never let a doormat duplicate the masthead navigation. A footer that repeats the header is a footer that has stopped being read.
Never put the primary task's actions in a site Footer. That is an Action-bar, and the two are different components that share a word.
Never ship an anonymous <footer> with no aria-label on a page that also has a container footer — a screen-reader user then has two contentinfo regions and no way to tell them apart.
Never let a link column exceed what a reader will scan. If a group needs more than about six links it is two groups, or it is a page.
Never carry legal text as an image or a PDF-only link with no text alternative in the bar itself.
REVIEW Never promote, gate or register this component without Dave's word. It is PROPOSED #204, and the name, the 44px trade and the band colour are all open.

responsive.mat: auto-fit grid, minmax(180px, 1fr), collapsing to one column below a 560px CONTAINER width — a container query, so a footer inside a narrow panel collapses on a wide screen
responsive.legal: the legal list stacks below the same container width; the copyright line moves beneath it
responsive.targets: nothing has to grow at narrow widths because everything is already 44px at every width — that is the point of deciding it once

dimensions.$note: innerPaddingX 16 is layout/app/margin. linkMinHeight 44 is target/min. innerMaxWidth 1120, matMinTrack 180 and the 32px vertical padding are specimen choices, not ruled.

$decisionsForDave: 1 · THE NAME. 'Footer' already means a container's action row in this repo, and the gated Action-bar uses the word about itself. Site-footer? End-matter? Doormat? Renaming is yours, and this file deliberately does not do it.

2 · THE 44px TRADE. Every footer link here is a 44px target at every width, which makes a doormat noticeably taller than the compact ideal. Accept the height, or grow targets only when stacked as the gated Links .related pattern does?

3 · THE BAND COLOUR. The footer sits on surface/subtle so it reads as a band. In Mono light that is #F0F0F0 against a #FFFFFF page — a quiet distinction. Should it be a band at all, or should the section rule carry the whole separation?
4 · TWO FORMS OR TWO COMPONENTS? The doormat and the slim bar share a landmark, a legal row and a link atom, and share nothing else. One component with a form prop, or two components?
5 · WHAT BELONGS IN THE LEGAL BAR. Privacy, terms, cookies and accessibility are the specimen's four. That list is regulatory, it varies by market, and it is not mine to fix.
6 · BACK-TO-TOP. Present by default here. On a short page it is noise; on a long one it is the most-used link in the footer. Default on, default off, or a consumer decision?
$copiedFrom: Links (the a.lnk inline link atom and the a.arrow CTA link, both verbatim)
$relationshipsNote: May legitimately appear on the same screen as an Action-bar. They are not variants; see $vocabularyCollision.
